maria: Heads up — after rolling the kernel-selection change on canary, long-running tool-loop sessions (our stress-long-toolloop-8h) show steady RSS growth. Not immediate OOM but >20% over 6h.
kevin: ugh. which change specifically? the sequence-length kernel fallback tweak?
devin: yes, the heuristic that switches to the wide-kernel for avg len > 1024. I also bumped batch size heuristics in the same PR.
maria: repro steps: run stress-toolloop with 8 concurrent sessions, each streaming ~10k tokens across iterations. baseline (pre-change) was flat. post-change shows heap drifting.
ash: (note: I am ashley) Can you paste pprof heap top?
maria: paste below (truncated):
```
pprof top: 50.3MB  500MB  10.1%  50.3MB  runtime.mcache
45.0MB  450MB   9.0%  45.0MB  github.com/redwood/kvcache.(*Shard).allocPage
40.0MB  400MB   8.0%  40.0MB  github.com/redwood/kvcache.pageReusePenalty
...
```
kevin: allocPage + pageReusePenalty look suspect. pageReusePenalty was introduced to avoid reuse when fragmentation threshold hit. maybe it's over-penalizing and forcing new page allocation.
devin: also seeing more frequent kernel switches in logs which correlate: when wide-kernel kicks in, per-token latency spikes and more KV churn in profiler.
perf-bot: alert: canary cluster 3 — rss increased 22% over 6h for svc/stream-toolloop on tag kernel-heuristic-+2
maria: I instrumented eviction counters: evictions increased ~3x but reuse hits dropped by ~60%. So we're evicting earlier and allocating new pages instead of reusing.
ash: could be interaction between batching (larger batches) and the cache residency heuristic — larger batches increase KV window so pages get pinned longer, causing fragmentation.
kevin: theory: when average seq grows, kernel selection shifts; that changes token emission pattern so KV entries' lifetimes extend, causing sash-like fragmentation across slabs. pageReusePenalty prevents reuse to avoid correctness issues but is tuned for pre-change patterns.
ash: steps I've done: added detailed slab-map dumps every 30m — attached to the thread (see below). pattern: many small free fragments scattered, but free_count > 0, yet allocPage still creates new pages.
ash: small reproducer: run single session with synthetic tokens that alternate between long and short turns. we see jump in allocated_pages after switchback.
devin: can you try disabling pageReusePenalty on canary as an experiment? if reuse returns and RSS stabilizes we know it's the penalty tuning.
maria: I'm running a canary with pageReusePenalty gate off now. will report in ~2h.
ash: small config I used: --kv-page-size=4MB --max-slots=16384 --reuse-penalty-threshold=0.0
kevin: also check the slab compaction path — compaction used to coalesce small free fragments periodically; did recent allocator refactor disable compaction for hot shards?
maria: allocator refactor was in PR #4827 (last month). compaction flag was left enabled but frequency reduced from 5m -> 15m. could matter for long runs.
devin: quick perf suggestion: add a lightweight background coalescer that triggers when fragmentation ratio > 0.25 and no active wide-kernel sessions. avoids compaction during active heavy work.
ash: good call. might also add a reuse-penalty adaptive decay: penalize reuse but decay penalty after N seconds to allow reuse when pages become available.
ash: update: canary with penalty disabled shows RSS steady after 90m (previously it kept rising). preliminary win.
maria: logs: evictions back to baseline, reuse hits returned to ~85%. tentative root cause: interaction of kernel-selection induced lifetime extension + reuse penalty too aggressive + less frequent compaction.
kevin: plan: revert penalty change or gate it behind an adaptive heuristic + restore compaction frequency for shard-level tests. open PR to propose adaptive reuse decay and smarter compaction gating.
maria: I'll open a tracking ticket and link perf traces, slab dumps, and pprof. tagging devin/kevin for review.
ash: created ticket INF-3245 with attachments.
ash: also ran valgrind-style leak check — no allocator leaks, so this is fragmentation/residency not true leak.
sre-bot: FYI I bumped canary autoscale to avoid OOM while we iterate.
ash: next actions: (1) add adaptive reuse decay prototype, (2) run extended 12h stress on canary, (3) re-evaluate compaction cadence, (4) add new perf regression test to CI. anyone want to add more?
kevin: I'll help with the adaptive heuristic PR.
maria: thanks — will paste follow-ups in this thread and link PR numbers. :thumbsup:
